description:
Add a section to the workspace AGENTS.md documenting the extras-preservation policy after JMAP-lbdy lands.

Suggested location: between the existing 'Sloppy-Value pattern for IETF-defined nested objects' section and the 'TLS stack' section. The new section's relationship to Sloppy-Value: Sloppy-Value is for IETF-spec'd nested objects (JSCalendar/JSContact/etc.) where the value SHAPE is owned by an external spec; extras is for vendor/site-private FIELDS that are not declared by any spec and just need to round-trip.

Required content (extras policy):
- Pattern: `pub extra: serde_json::Map<String, Value>` with `#[serde(flatten, default, skip_serializing_if = "serde_json::Map::is_empty")]`.
- Why: vendor/site fields in production JMAP deployments add data without waiting for IETF process. Silent-drop is the spec floor (RFC 8620 §1.6); workspace policy is preservation.
- Scope: every public Deserialize struct that appears on the JMAP wire. NOT internal Rust API types (backend trait results, mock backends, parsing helpers, test fixtures).
- Test discipline: every in-scope type has at least one round-trip preservation test asserting unknown fields survive serialize.
- Field shape and visibility (pub field, lowercase `extra`).
- New types added to any in-scope crate MUST include extras from day one.

Required content (filter-algebra exclusion — added 2026-05-10):
A sub-section explaining that **filter and comparator algebra types and control string enums are explicitly OUT of the extras policy**. This must cover:

- The three exclusions: (a) Filter<T> / FilterOperator<T> and per-crate FilterCondition types; (b) Comparator types (EmailComparator, CalendarEventComparator, etc.); (c) control string enums (Operator, ComparatorProperty).
- Rationale (cross-reference JMAP-lbdy "Decision: filter algebra excluded"):
  1. Silent-drop foot-gun at server — an unknown filter clause silently round-tripping through the client creates query-correctness bugs (wrong result sets returned with no compile-time or runtime signal).
  2. `Filter<T>` is `#[serde(untagged)]` over a fixed variant set — extras on the condition struct cannot introduce new variant shapes.
  3. Control enums must dispatch on known variants — `Unknown(String)` is meaningless for `Operator` (AND/OR/NOT) and `ComparatorProperty`; backends cannot honor unrecognised values. `#[non_exhaustive]` already gives spec-level forward-compat.
- **Future hook — IETF-track path**: vendors needing capability-declared, filterable extras should use `draft-ietf-jmap-metadata` (currently draft-01, capability URI `urn:ietf:params:jmap:metadata`). It defines a companion Annotation object keyed by `(relatedType, relatedId)`, with schema discovery via the capability's `dataTypes` / `metadataTypes` / `maxDepth` properties and a `Metadata/query` filter (currently `textMatch` over vendor string properties — coarse but standardised). The workspace tracker for implementation is JMAP-06zp.
- **Future hook — pre-IETF escape**: vendors who need typed filter construction against custom server fields RIGHT NOW (before the metadata draft stabilises) can use the sloppy-value escape (`serde_json::Value` for the filter tree) or fork the per-crate `FilterCondition` type. The hybrid pattern documented in `crate-jmap-calendars-types/PLAN.md` is the model.
- Cross-reference: per-crate rustdoc on each in-scope filter/comparator/control-enum type carries the same exclusion + dual-future-hook notice (see JMAP-9wh7 for the propagation epic).

Acceptance: AGENTS.md updated with both sections (extras policy AND filter-algebra exclusion with dual future-hook guidance); cross-reference from each migrated crate's AGENTS.md (where applicable) and PLAN.md.
title: Document extras policy in workspace AGENTS.md
